A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MetaSpatial by the same authors. All 11 pages of v1 and 20 pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables, references, and v2's appendices, are readable. V1 contains no appendices.

before.justification: V1 reports original layout-generation experiments, reward ablations, refinement-depth comparisons, and qualitative examples in Section 3 and Tables 1–3.

after.justification: V2 reports original layout-generation experiments and additional spatial-question-answering, reasoning-trace, and SFT experiments in Section 3 and Appendices F–G.

M1.justification: Section 2.6 replaces the GRPO formulation with 3D-SPO, introducing object-specific physics modulation of coordinate-token advantages alongside trajectory-level rewards. This changes policy optimization rather than merely renaming GRPO. Section 3.5 also introduces an optional SFT warm-start procedure using high-reward layouts.

E1.justification: V2 adds Open3DVQA evaluation covering qualitative and quantitative spatial questions in urban environments, extending beyond indoor layout generation to a distinct task and domain. Appendix C's description of 10,000 indoor scenes documents the training data; it does not establish that the indoor dataset changed.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds GPT-4o, I-Design, and LayoutGPT to the original Qwen comparisons. New comparisons also include GPT-4, LLaVA-7B, and Qwen-VL-7B-SFT on Open3DVQA, plus SFT and hybrid training strategies in Table 7. The existing PPO and GRPO comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: Added protocols include zero-shot Open3DVQA evaluation using success rates and absolute relative errors, T=7 refinement settings, and pseudo-SFT selection above reward 0.8 followed by 100-step RL evaluations. Section 2.5 also revises the reported perceptual-scoring procedure to hold the color/material grade fixed. Single-turn final evaluation is newly explicit, without establishing that v1 used multi-turn testing.

E4.justification: V2 expands the depth study into matched GRPO/3D-SPO comparisons through T=7, adds reasoning-trace removal controls, and analyzes training efficiency and SFT warm starts. These test additional mechanisms and tradeoffs beyond v1's reward-component and refinement-depth ablations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. V2's group standard deviation is part of policy optimization, not experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V1's headline 7B results—GPT-4o score 0.58, collision 13.7%, and constraint violations 76.2%—remain as GRPO results in v2 Table 3. V2 Table 1 instead reports 3D-SPO results of 0.62, 11.5%, and 70.8%, so this is not an unchanged-method performance update. V2 also adds external-baseline, T=7, reasoning-trace, SFT, and Open3DVQA results.

T1.justification: Section 2.6 substantively reformulates the mathematics: v1's per-layout discounted reward surrogate becomes a discounted trajectory aggregate with coordinate-dependent, group-normalized advantages and a token-level clipped objective. These are changed mathematical definitions and optimization expressions, although neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list shift the central innovation from multi-turn refinement using GRPO to the proposed 3D-SPO algorithm, emphasizing object-level physics modulation and temporal credit assignment during training. V2 also removes the conclusion's explicit claim of improved generation diversity over supervised approaches.

C2.justification: V2 qualifies the earlier increasing-depth interpretation with degradation at T=7, attributed to over-adjustment or reward saturation. It adds explanations of training efficiency and reasoning-trace benefits, and recognizes SFT as useful initialization despite its limitations as standalone training. Appendix C also explicitly identifies single-room and static-lighting boundaries.

D1.justification: V2 newly documents dataset construction, asset retrieval and filtering, collision processing, Blender settings, generation and evaluation prompts, and staged reward training. It clarifies initial empty-room inputs and single-turn testing. Conversely, v1's specification of four H100 GPUs disappears; the stated public repository remains unchanged.

R1.justification: The three-part related-work survey is largely retained in Appendix B. V2 adds focused references including DeepSeekMath, OpenShape, Open3DVQA, and VLM2-Bench, and explicitly distinguishes 3D-SPO from standard GRPO. The broader positioning as an RL framework for VLM-based 3D layout generation remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method descriptions, optimization section, and conclusion undergo extensive rewriting. Related work moves from the main text to Appendix B, while a dedicated SFT section, acknowledgments, and organized appendices substantially restructure the document.

P2.justification: V2 adds GRPO/3D-SPO and coordinate-masking diagrams, expands Tables 1 and 3, and introduces Tables 4–7, prompt listings, and additional scene illustrations. The original before/after montage is retained as Figure 4 rather than new evidence. Typography, headings, captions, and page layout are also restyled.

improvement.justification: V2 materially addresses v1's lack of direct scene-generator and SFT comparisons, adds matched GRPO/3D-SPO ablations, and supplies substantial dataset, rendering, and prompt documentation. These additions strengthen empirical support and reproducibility beyond merely reporting higher scores. The gains outweigh the removed hardware detail and reporting weaknesses, including Table 7's inconsistent constraint-direction label; incomplete evaluation protocols and absent uncertainty estimates remain limitations.
